subject: Rossum PoC: model fit, evals & compression options

To: Simon Park <simon.park@rossum.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rossum PoC: model fit, evals & compression options

Hi Simon —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Goal: proof-of-concept to validate retrieval+LLM extraction on Rossum's invoice line-item data (target latency <= 120ms p50 for single-request flow; target throughput 50 qps for batch ingestion).

2) Preliminary model candidates: small Llama-variant for high throughput (7B-q8), and a mid-size instruction-tuned Llama/Redwood-verified 13B baseline for quality-sensitive flows.

3) Evaluation plan (attached):
   - We’ll run the prompt set you shared through baseline float32 run, then AWQ and GPTQ quantized variants to measure f1/precision/recall on the extraction task and per-token latency/cost.
   - Deliverables: summary of model-fit (accuracy vs latency), prompt-set failure modes, and a short playbook with suggested quantization profiles.

4) Security & procurement: you mentioned needing an internal SOC2 questionnaire — Laura will follow up with the package and a timeline for Dedicated/private options.

Ask for you: please confirm the data slice (sample size ~1k PDFs) and whether we can access via a secure S3 share by EOD Thurs. Once we have data we’ll queue a 72-hour run for the evals.

Attachments: rossum_prompt_set_v1.txt, rossum_eval_results_baseline.csv (placeholder), quant_tradeoff_onepager.pdf

Next steps:
- Simon: confirm data share + procurement contacts
- Redwood (Hannah/Rishi): kick off baseline eval + quantization matrix once sample is live

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers:
- Confirmed: we can provision a secure S3 bucket (1k sample invoices, mixed layouts) and give read-only keys. I’ll send the link once IT finishes the ACLs (expect EOD Thu).
- Latency target is correct; throughput target may need flexibility during the PoC while you tune batching and KV caching — we’ll accept a staged improvement plan.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you call out where AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 tend to introduce extraction regressions vs float32 (concrete failure modes)?
2) Rough cost delta for an AWQ+7B flow vs 13B fp16 baseline (ballpark monthly token cost assuming our expected call volume).

If possible, can Rishi or another engineer provide a short doc summarizing the quantization tradeoffs for extraction tasks? That would help our procurement/engineering align.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon.park@rossum.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Rossum PoC: model fit, evals & compression options

Simon —

Thanks for the call and the follow-ups. I put together a short tradeoffs note below (attaching a one-pager). High level answers first, then quick technical context:

High level:
- AWQ (per-token int8-ish schemes) tends to preserve instruction-following behavior well for many decoder-only LMs and gives the best cost/latency upside with minimal quality drop for extraction tasks when prompts are stable.
- GPTQ-style methods (per-channel quant) can be slightly better for very small models where weight distribution varies, but they require careful calibration and can be brittle across prompt variants.
- FP8 (upcoming on some runtimes) offers float-like quality at reduced memory but currently has runtime availability constraints and less mature toolchains.

Concrete failure modes we’ll watch for during evals:
- Numeric bleed on delimiter tokens leading to merged fields (AWQ edge-case under long KV cache).
- Tokenization shifts causing label misalignment (rare, but more visible in heavy abbreviation cases).
- Subtle hallucination on low-frequency vendor names when switching to aggressive quantization on 7B variants.

Recommended experiment matrix (we’ll run these automatically):
- Baseline: 13B fp16 (quality target)
- Candidate A: 7B AWQ (low-cost candidate)
- Candidate B: 7B GPTQ calibrated (stability check)
- Candidate C: 13B GPTQ (if we need middle ground for quality with cost savings)

Measurement plan:
- Task metrics: extraction F1, field-level precision/recall, and slot-level exact match
- Latency: p50/p90 per flow (single-request), throughput (qps) under our batching profile
- Cost: per-1000-requests token + infra spend estimate (we’ll provide a ballpark in the PoC report)

Links/benchmarks:
- PoC folder and run configs: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Rossum-PoC-2027
- Internal batch benchmark run: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/runs/R-2027-045

Rough cost delta (very approximate):
- 13B fp16 baseline: 1.0x cost baseline
- 7B AWQ: ~0.35–0.5x cost depending on token counts and batching efficiency
- 7B GPTQ: ~0.4–0.55x (higher calibration overhead)

I’ll kick off an automated run once the S3 sample is available. Expect a 48–72 hour initial turnaround for the matrix above; results will include fail-case examples and recommended prompt-set adjustments.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

This looks good. We’ll provision the S3 sample today and I’ll PM the link to Hannah once ACLs are set. The 48–72 hour run timeline works for us.

Please include at least 5 representative failure examples in the deliverable so our QA team can triage quickly. Also, Laura, please send the SOC2 package when you have a minute — procurement wants to get that ahead of the pilot.

Simon
